name: AI Automation with Python Handbook
tagline: From LLM APIs to production agents. Build, deploy and monitor real AI automations with Python and n8n: prompts, structured outputs, tool calling, embeddings, OpenAI/Claude/Gemini/Groq, LiteLLM, Ollama, n8n, Make, Zapier, LangChain, RAG and vector databases, LangGraph, CrewAI, agent SDKs, MCP and A2A, Gmail/Slack/WhatsApp bots, browser and voice agents, Celery/Prefect/Temporal, Streamlit, Docker, Langfuse, evals, and LLM security — with mini projects, Mermaid and SVG diagrams, and a capstone.

journey.conceptChallenge: Explain how you would use {name} in a real business automation, and name one way it fails in production.
journey.practiceIntro: Plan a real automation end to end. Talk through each step aloud — trigger, model, tools, data, failure modes — then open the chapter to compare.
journey.practiceDrillIntro: Work through each step. Tick items as you cover them, then compare with the full chapter.
practiceSteps: Who triggers it, what input arrives, what output is 'done', and what must never happen (wrong email sent, data leaked).
Can the steps be fixed in advance? Prefer a deterministic workflow; use an agent only for open-ended steps.
Model per step by difficulty, latency and cost; a fallback provider; local model if data cannot leave.
System prompt, few-shot examples, Pydantic output schemas, tool definitions.
Which data does it need? RAG over which sources, chunking, retrieval quality checks.
Triggers, webhooks, APIs (Gmail, Slack, CRM), MCP servers, n8n vs Python boundary.
Retries, idempotency, queues, schedules, caching, rate limits, human approval for risky actions.
Secrets, least-privilege tools, prompt-injection defences, PII redaction, sandboxing.
Docker, CI with evals, tracing (Langfuse/LangSmith), cost dashboards, alerting.

homeIntro:
You already know Python, APIs and data. This handbook turns that into AI automations that run unattended in production: LLM APIs, n8n, RAG, agents, MCP, integrations, scheduling, deployment, monitoring and security.
10
Parts
44
Chapters
5
Appendices
44
Mini projects

Every chapter follows the same 10 steps: overview, key concepts, setup, runnable Python 3.11+ code, a real business use case, a 1–2 hour mini project, a comparison table, mistakes & best practices, exercises with self-check questions, and links to the official docs. Free and open-source first (Ollama, Chroma, self-hosted n8n); paid options are named alongside. For the theory underneath (transformers, training, fine-tuning) see the AI Engineering handbook.

items.name: How LLMs Work: Tokens, Context, Temperature, Hallucinations & Cost
items.summary: The working model an automation engineer needs: tokens, context windows, sampling and temperature, why models hallucinate, and how to estimate and control cost before you ship.

items.name: Prompt Engineering: System Prompts, Few-Shot & Chain-of-Thought
items.summary: Prompts as code: system prompts, few-shot examples, delimiters, chain-of-thought vs reasoning models, prompt templates, versioning and a regression harness.

items.name: Structured Outputs: Reliable JSON with Pydantic
items.summary: From 'please reply in JSON' to schema-constrained decoding: JSON mode, json_schema / strict structured outputs, Pydantic models, Instructor, validation and repair loops.

items.name: Function Calling & Tool Use
items.summary: How models request your functions: tool schemas, the tool-use loop, parallel calls, errors, tool choice, and safe execution — the foundation of every agent.

items.name: Embeddings & Semantic Similarity
items.summary: Text as vectors: embedding models, cosine similarity, normalisation, batching, dimensions and cost — semantic search, dedup, clustering and routing without a vector DB.

items.name: Model APIs: OpenAI, Claude, Gemini & Groq
items.summary: The four API families you will meet in production: their SDKs, request shapes, streaming, errors and rate limits — and a thin provider-neutral client you own.

items.name: Multi-Provider Routing: LiteLLM & OpenRouter
items.summary: One interface, many models: LiteLLM SDK and proxy, OpenRouter, fallbacks, load balancing, cost-based routing, budgets and virtual keys.

items.name: Local Models: Ollama & Hugging Face
items.summary: Run models on your own hardware: Ollama, its OpenAI-compatible endpoint, quantisation and VRAM, Hugging Face transformers and Inference Providers — and when local is worth it.

items.name: n8n: Triggers, Nodes, AI Agent Node, Code Node, Webhooks & Self-Hosting
items.summary: Self-hosted workflow automation: triggers, nodes and items, expressions, the AI Agent node with tools and memory, the Code node, webhooks, credentials and Docker deployment.

items.name: Make, Zapier & Power Automate
items.summary: The SaaS automation platforms: scenarios, zaps and flows, AI steps, pricing models, limits and governance — and how they compare to n8n.

items.name: Flowise, Langflow & Dify
items.summary: Visual LLM app builders: drag-and-drop chains, RAG and agents, their APIs, self-hosting, and when to graduate to code.

items.name: Connecting n8n with Python Scripts
items.summary: Hybrid automation: n8n calling FastAPI services, Python calling n8n webhooks, Execute Command, queues, auth, and where each piece of logic should live.

items.name: LangChain Core: Prompts, Chains (LCEL) & Output Parsers
items.summary: LangChain's building blocks: chat models, prompt templates, the Runnable interface and LCEL, output parsers, structured output, streaming and batching.

items.name: LangChain Tools & Agents
items.summary: Tools as Python functions, tool-calling models, create_agent, middleware, and how LangChain agents relate to LangGraph.

items.name: Document Loaders & Text Splitters
items.summary: Getting documents into LLM-sized pieces: loaders for PDFs, web, Office and databases; recursive, token, markdown and semantic splitters; metadata.

items.name: RAG Fundamentals: Chunking, Embeddings & Retrieval
items.summary: The full retrieval-augmented generation pipeline: ingest, chunk, embed, store, retrieve, generate with citations — and the failure modes at each step.

items.name: Reranking & Hybrid Search
items.summary: Beyond top-k cosine: BM25 + vector hybrid search, reciprocal rank fusion, cross-encoder reranking, query rewriting, HyDE and multi-query.

items.name: Vector Databases: Chroma, FAISS, Qdrant, Pinecone & pgvector
items.summary: Where embeddings live: ANN indexes (HNSW, IVF), filtering, persistence, scaling and cost — five stores compared with the same code.

items.name: LlamaIndex & Haystack
items.summary: Two RAG-first frameworks: LlamaIndex indexes, query engines and workflows; Haystack pipelines and components — compared with LangChain.

items.name: Document Parsing: PyMuPDF, Unstructured & Docling
items.summary: Garbage in, garbage out: extracting text, tables and layout from PDFs and Office files, OCR fallbacks, and parsing at scale.

items.name: Agent Patterns: ReAct, Planning & Reflection
items.summary: How agents think: the ReAct loop, plan-and-execute, reflection and self-critique, stopping conditions, and when a workflow beats an agent.

items.name: Agent Memory & Mem0
items.summary: Short-term vs long-term memory, summarisation, semantic memory stores, Mem0 for user-level memory, and privacy of remembered data.

items.name: LangGraph: State, Nodes & Edges
items.summary: Agents as graphs: typed state, reducers, nodes, conditional edges, cycles, tool nodes, subgraphs and streaming.

items.name: LangGraph in Production: Checkpoints & Human-in-the-Loop
items.summary: Durable agents: checkpointers, threads, interrupts and approvals, time travel, persistence with Postgres, and deployment.

items.name: CrewAI: Roles, Tasks & Crews
items.summary: Role-based multi-agent teams: agents, tasks, crews, processes, flows, tools and memory — with an honest look at cost and control.

items.name: OpenAI Agents SDK, Claude Agent SDK & Google ADK
items.summary: The model vendors' agent frameworks: agents, handoffs, guardrails and tracing; Claude Code as a library; Google's Agent Development Kit — compared.

items.name: PydanticAI, AutoGen/AG2, smolagents & DSPy
items.summary: Four more philosophies: type-safe agents, conversational multi-agent, code-writing agents, and programming (not prompting) LLMs.

items.name: MCP: Building Model Context Protocol Servers with FastMCP
items.summary: The USB-C of AI tools: MCP hosts, clients and servers, tools/resources/prompts, transports, building servers with FastMCP, auth and security.

items.name: A2A: The Agent-to-Agent Protocol
items.summary: How independent agents discover and delegate to each other: agent cards, tasks, messages, artifacts, streaming — and how A2A complements MCP.

items.name: Gmail, Google Workspace & Microsoft 365
items.summary: Automating email, calendars, docs and sheets: OAuth, service accounts, Gmail and Graph APIs, push notifications, and AI triage pipelines.

items.name: Telegram, WhatsApp, Slack & Discord Bots
items.summary: AI assistants where users already are: bot APIs, webhooks vs polling, message formats, rate limits and conversation state.

items.name: Browser Agents: Playwright & browser-use
items.summary: Automating the web: deterministic Playwright scripts, LLM-driven browser agents, selectors vs vision, anti-bot reality and safety.

items.name: Voice: Whisper, ElevenLabs, Vapi & Retell
items.summary: Speech in, speech out: transcription, text-to-speech, real-time voice agents, latency budgets and telephony.

items.name: OCR & Multimodal Vision
items.summary: Reading images and documents: Tesseract and cloud OCR versus vision LLMs, invoice and receipt extraction, and accuracy checks.

items.name: RPA: UiPath & pyautogui
items.summary: When there is no API: robotic process automation, desktop scripting with pyautogui, UiPath, and adding AI to legacy workflows.

items.name: Cron, APScheduler & Celery + Redis
items.summary: Running automations on time and in the background: cron, APScheduler, Celery workers with Redis, retries and idempotency.

items.name: Prefect, Airflow & Temporal
items.summary: Orchestrating multi-step pipelines: DAGs, flows, durable execution, retries and observability — which orchestrator for which job.

items.name: UIs for AI Apps: Streamlit, Gradio & Chainlit
items.summary: Putting a face on an automation: chat UIs, file upload, streaming, auth and sharing — three frameworks compared.

items.name: Deployment: Docker, Cloud/VPS Hosting & GitHub Actions
items.summary: Shipping AI services: Dockerfiles for Python AI apps, VPS vs PaaS vs serverless, secrets, and CI/CD with evals in the pipeline.

items.name: Monitoring: LangSmith & Langfuse
items.summary: Seeing inside LLM apps: traces, spans, prompts, token and cost tracking, user feedback, datasets — hosted and self-hosted.

items.name: Evaluation: RAGAS, DeepEval & promptfoo
items.summary: Proving your automation works: golden datasets, LLM-as-judge, RAG metrics, regression tests in CI and red-teaming.

items.name: Caching, Rate Limits, Retries & Cost Tracking
items.summary: Production hardening: prompt and response caching, backoff, circuit breakers, concurrency limits, budgets and per-feature cost attribution.

items.name: Prompt Injection & Sandboxing Code Execution
items.summary: The top LLM risk: direct and indirect injection, the lethal trifecta, defence in depth, least privilege, and running model-written code safely.

items.name: Secrets Management & PII Handling
items.summary: Keeping keys and personal data safe: env vars, secret managers, rotation, PII detection and redaction with Presidio, retention and compliance.

items.name: Appendix A · Glossary of AI Automation Terms
items.summary: Every term used in the handbook, defined in one or two plain sentences with a link to its home chapter.

items.name: Appendix B · Cheat Sheet: Key Commands & Snippets
items.summary: One-screen reference: install commands, env vars, the canonical snippet for each SDK and framework, and Docker one-liners.

items.name: Appendix C · 10 Portfolio Project Ideas
items.summary: Ten projects from beginner to advanced, each with scope, stack, stretch goals and what it proves to an employer or client.

items.name: Appendix D · Capstone: n8n + LangGraph + RAG + MCP, Deployed
items.summary: An end-to-end support-operations automation: n8n intake, a LangGraph agent with RAG and MCP tools, human approval, Docker deployment, tracing and evals.

items.name: Appendix E · 12-Week Learning Roadmap
items.summary: A week-by-week plan through the handbook with hours, deliverables and checkpoints.
